name: Biwat
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: McElvenny, James 2006. Draft sketch grammar of Biwat (Mudukumo/Mundugumor); Mead 1932 Mundugumor Linguistics — not found online

sources.citation: Barlow, Russell. 2023. A grammar of Ulwa (Papua New Guinea). Berlin: Language Science Press. (consulted held by the project at for its citations of McElvenny 2006)
sources.note: Not a Biwat description; cites 'McElvenny, James. 2006. Notes on the Mudukumo language of the Yuat River, East Sepik Province, PNG. Univ. of Sydney, unpublished MS' (pp. 18, 29, 43, 60; p. 60 = phonemic voiced labiodental in Mundukumo). Says nothing about Mundukumo stress.

sources.citation: OLAC: Resources in and about the Biwat language (language-archives.org/language/bwm, the Internet Archive 2023 capture)
sources.note: Inventory only: PARADISEC JM1 (McElvenny 2005-06 audio), DL1-093 Laycock 1973 Biwat fieldnotes, DL2-034 Laycock Notebook D23, transnewguinea.org wordlists, Ethnologue. No SIL phonology/OPD item exists for bwm.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Mundugumor language' (consonant and vowel inventory cited to Foley 2018)
sources.note: Lists consonants /p t k mb nd ndʒ ŋg m n ɲ ŋ f s mv r w j/ and vowels /i u e ə o a/ after Foley 2018; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: SIL-PNG, PNG Language Resources: Biwat [bwm] (pnglanguages.org, the Internet Archive 2016 capture)
sources.note: 'Nothing yet available' -- no Organised Phonology Data, survey report or grammar for Biwat.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2005. Linguistic prehistory in the Sepik-Ramu basin. In A. Pawley et al. (eds.), Papuan Pasts, 109-144. Pacific Linguistics 572. (hdl 1885/146735)
sources.note: Mentions Biwat, Bun, Miyak pronouns and plural suffix -bi to argue Yuat is unrelated to Lower Sepik-Ramu; no phonology, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. & J. Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, 731-763. Pacific Linguistics C-38. (hdl 1885/252975)
sources.note: Phylum-wide feature list (p. 732) includes only 'lack of complex suprasegmental systems'; sec. 2.11.3.5.1 Yuat Super-Stock (p. 758) is classification only; no Biwat phonology, no stress statement.
sources.venue: New Guinea area languages and language study 1

sources.citation: transnewguinea.org, Biwat language page (sources SIL 1975 'Language survey of Biwat', SIL 1976)
sources.note: Survey wordlists only (171 items); no prosodic information.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU. (hdl 1885/146478)
sources.note: Entry 127 Biwat (p. 37) gives villages, names (Mundokuma, Mundugumor), test list; Yuat stock paragraph (pp. 36-37) is typological/lexical only. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: McElvenny, James. 2006. Draft sketch grammar of Biwat (Mudukumo/Mundugumor), a Yuat language of East Sepik Province, PNG [cited by Barlow 2023 as 'Notes on the Mudukumo language of the Yuat River, East Sepik Province, PNG', Univ. of Sydney, unpublished MS]. 62 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only modern description of Biwat; Barlow 2023 cites its p. 60 for phoneme facts, so it has a phonology section that very likely states stress. Copies held by W. Foley, R. Barlow, and the Glottolog/hh collection; author (now Univ. Siegen) reachable at james.mcelvenny@mailbox.org.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher
sources.note: Yuat-family section summarises Mundukumo (Biwat) phonology from McElvenny 2006; the most likely published (second-hand) place for a Biwat stress remark.
sources.venue: The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide
